jamie: quick run — microbench for KV-cache prefetch with paged+fused flash variants across A100 / H100 / L40S. TL;DR: prefetch cuts tail on H100 for bs>=8 & seq>=4096, but increases median on L40S for small batches. sending details + raw numbers. cc @sasha @rao

sasha: nice. did you compare against no-prefetch and plain paged-flash? what kernel-selection policy was used?

jamie: yes. compared 3 configs: no-prefetch, prefetch (background kvcache fetch next 512 tokens), and prefetch-1024. kernel policy = auto-v2 (prefers flash_paged, fallback flash_fused). bench command i used: `./bench/attn_bench --kernel flash_paged_prefetch --hw h100 --bs 8 --seq 4096 --runs 50`

rao: can you paste median/p95/p99 numbers + any kernel launch overhead diffs?

jamie: short numbers (all ms, mean of 50 runs):
H100 (bs=8, seq=4096):
median: 82ms (no-prefetch 85ms)
p95: 160ms (no-prefetch 210ms)
p99: 230ms (no-prefetch 400ms)
GPU util: +4%

A100 (bs=8, seq=4096):
median: 95ms (no-prefetch 92ms)
p95: 220ms (no-prefetch 240ms)
p99: 320ms (no-prefetch 360ms)
GPU util: +2%

L40S (bs=8, seq=4096):
median: 150ms (no-prefetch 140ms)  <-- regression
p95: 260ms (no-prefetch 290ms)
p99: 410ms (no-prefetch 420ms)
notes: L40S p95/p99 improved slightly but median regressed, likely due to extra memcpy / scheduling overhead for small microbatches.

marie: interesting — L40S median regression suggests prefetch overhead during cache warmup. did you capture nvtx/nsys traces? any memcpy spikes?

jamie: yes, nvtx shows host->device memcpy spikes ~0.6-0.9ms per prefetch op; on L40S PCIe scheduling stalls increase for bs<=4. SM utilization improved on H100 (fewer idle cycles), but on L40S the prefetch memcpy costs outweighed compute gains for small batches. perf counters: increased HtoD bytes and reduced SM idle on H100.

perf-bot: bench CI: job 542 completed, artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/1812349999/ (nsys traces, csvs, kernel logs)

sasha: next steps i suggest:
1) adaptive prefetch threshold by (hw, bs, seq) — enable only when ms_saved_estimate > memcpy_cost_estimate
2) sweep prefetch size (256/512/1024) and prefetch distance (next 512/1024 tokens)
3) run larger bs sweep (1,2,4,8,16,32,64) and seq sweep (512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384) on Dedicated pool canary

jamie: implementing adaptive heuristic. quick patch idea:
```
if (seq > 2048 && bs >= 8 && hw == H100) {
  prefetch_size = 512;
} else {
  prefetch_size = 0;
}
```
will add cost estimator based on measured memcpy bandwidth and kernel speedup.

rao: please open a PR with the patch + full perf traces and kernel selection logs. tag eng-runtime + eng-ml. include a test that flips policy in CI.

jamie: opened PR #6252 with initial adaptive heuristic + bench harness. uploading full traces now.

dev-bot: CI: PR 6252 — unit tests + microbench passed (flaky thresholds disabled for main CI).

jamie: :thumbsup: thanks all. i'll run extended sweep this week and post consolidated dashboard (p95/p99 heatmaps by hw/bs/seq). scheduling follow-up sync next wed.
